topic: How event loops work in Node.js

beats.narration: Node-J-S runs your code on one single thread. So how does it handle thousands of requests at once without blocking?
Your synchronous code runs on the call stack, one frame at a time. Nothing else runs until that stack is empty.
Async work, like file reads or timers, gets handed off to libuv's thread pool or the O-S, running completely off the main thread.
When that work finishes, its callback waits in a queue. Promises skip that queue entirely and go straight into a microtask queue instead.
The event loop watches the call stack. The moment it's empty, it drains the microtask queue completely, then pulls just one callback from the other queue.
One thread, one call stack. The real work happens elsewhere, and the event loop just brings the results back, in order.
